question.leadin: In 1962, this man was imprisoned for life at Robben Island.
question.text: Name this civil rights leader who became the first black president of South Africa.
question.clue: Percy Yutar oversaw this man's prosecution in the Rivonia Trial, in which he was convicted for his leadership of Spear of the Nation.

swap.leadin: This policy was reinforced by the Bantu Education Act.
swap.text: Name this policy, which Stephen Biko protested in South Africa. It called for the racial segregation of blacks and whites.
swap.clue: It became harsher during Hendrik Verwoerd's prime ministership with the creation of ten Bantustan "homelands."

question.leadin: This African empire had its capital at Gao.
question.text: Name this West African empire that dominated the region in the 15th and 16th centuries. Its rulers included Askia.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about African Imperialism.
swap.text: This battle was a part of Britain's attempt to reconquer Sudan. General Herbert Kitchener defeated a much larger Sudanese army with help of modern weapons such as the Gatling Gun.
swap.clue: The main commander here was forced to depart soon after to tend to the Fashoda Incident.

question.text: The Evian Accords provided independence for this former French colony in North Africa.
question.clue: Ahmed Ben Bella served as the first president of this country after a war that led to many pieds-noirs ("p'yay-NWAR") fleeing this country.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about French attempts to colonize Africa.
swap.text: This country was the site of a border dispute between the French and British in its city of Fashoda. Lord Kitchener defeated the Mahdist forces at the Battle of Omdurman in this country.
swap.clue: General Marchand marched his forces to Fashoda in this country during one incident here.

question.leadin: Answer the following about 14th century west Africa.
question.text: This west African nation was founded by Sundiata Keita, and constructed many mosques and universities in Timbuktu.
question.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.text: The Almoravids, like the Almohads, kept their capital in this modern day country. This country's Rif Region was historically occupied by its northern neighbor.
swap.clue: This non-European nation saw a period of repression called the "Years of Lead" during the reign of Hassan II, which saw the assassination of native activist Mehdi Ben Barka.

question.leadin: In the February 1896 Battle of Adowa, about seventy percent of General Oreste Baratieri's men were casualties.
question.text: Baratieri was leading an Italian invasion of this country, which successfully repelled the Italians in 1896 but suffered a second confrontation as part of World War II.
question.clue: The Hayamots helped Gebre Lalibela's line defeat Queen Gudit, who had ended a golden age that saw this country defeat Dhu Nuwas and the Himyarites and take control of Yemen.

swap.text: Mengistu overthrew this emperor of Ethiopia who called on the League of Nations to help repel a foreign invasion of his country prior to World War II.
swap.answerHtml: Haile Selassie I [accept Ras Tafari Makonnen; prompt on Haile or Selassie; prompt on Makonnen; prompt on Tafari]
swap.clue: From 1936 to 1941, this leader lived outside of his country because it was occupied by Italy during what became known as the Abyssinia Crisis.

question.text: Longtime Ivorian president Felix Houphouet-Boigny ["oo-foo-EH bwahn-YEE"] moved the capital to Yamoussoukro from this city, which remains the most populous in Cote d'Ivoire.
question.clue: This was the capital of Cote d'Ivoire from 1933 to 1983, succeeding Bingerville in that role, and remains by far its largest city, with over three million residents.

swap.leadin: The French expeditionary forces at this incident were led by Jean-Baptiste Marchand.
swap.text: Identify this 1898 diplomatic crisis in which France and Britain vied for control of the title location in East Africa, which the French hoped would push Britain out of the region.
swap.clue: Resolved by a 1904 entente signed by Theodore Delcasse, it was caused by Gabriel Hanotaux ordering a force to march from Gabon to the namesake town, now called Kodok.

question.text: This anti-communist led UNITA during Angola's civil war. His death led to the end of the conflict.
question.clue: This man praised the Heritage Foundation for its role in repealing the Clark Amendment.

swap.leadin: The British army won many victories, but it also suffered many crushing defeats.
swap.text: Trouble with ammunition may have contributed to the decisive British defeat at Isandlwana, which was the opening engagement in a war fought against these peoples.
swap.clue: A leader of this ethnicity began the Mfecane ("mm-fuh-CAH-nay") when his impi warriors equipped with cowhide shields and iklwa ("ick-lwah") spears began conquering other Nguni kingdoms.

question.leadin: Yoweri Museveni and Paul Kagame helped one leader with this last name seize power, before invading again the next year in an attempt to overthrow him.
question.text: Give this last name of Laurent-Desire, who became the leader of his country in 1997, and his son Joseph, who took power after his father was assassinated in 2001 by a former child soldier.
question.clue: Another leader with this surname is opposed by figures including the convicted war criminal Jean-Pierre Bemba and Moise Katumbi.

swap.leadin: Name these African cities, none of which are national capitals.
swap.text: This is the third most populous city in Morocco after Casablanca and Marrakesh. It is home to the Al-Karaouine University, and much of its commercial activity occurs in its "new city" area.
swap.clue: A rich woman named Fatima al-Fahri founded a center of learning in this city, whose most sacred site is a shrine dedicated to Idriss II.

question.leadin: According to legend, a politician from this political party, which allied with Abdulrahman Mohamad Babu's far-left Umma Party, became an evil spirit called the popobawa upon his 1972 assassination.
question.text: Name this political party that merged with TANU after the death of its leader Abeid Karume ("uh-BAYD kah-ROO-may"). Its bloody overthrow of Jamshid ("jam-SHEED") bin ʿAbdullah was led on the ground by, inexplicably, the Christian fanatic John Okello.

swap.text: The United States led from behind in this operation to support the Libyan rebels in 2011. The United States would end this mission after 13 days and hand control over to NATO.

question.text: For her efforts, Gbowee won the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize along with this woman, who became the first modern African head of state after Charles Taylor's resignation following the peace talks.
question.clue: This politician who lost to Charles Taylor in 1997 but defeated George Weah (WEE-uh) in 2005 to become the first elected female head of state in Africa.

swap.leadin: This state was led by the Walashma dynasty like its predecessor, the Ifat sultanate.
swap.text: Identify this sultanate located on the western shores of the Gulf of Aden. Its general Ahmad Ibrahim al-Ghazi led several successful campaigns against Ethiopia and killed Emperor Dawit II.
swap.clue: This sultanate that fortified its "holy city" of Harar after Lebna Dengel allied Ethiopia with Portugal to fight its Afar and Somali forces. It was based north of the Ajuran Empire.
